findings: Buys: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it bought trailed SPY by 0.90% on average (49 buys, 41% of them ahead of SPY; t = -1.7, within noise).
Sells: over the five trading days from the fill, the stocks it sold beat SPY by 0.37%, so selling gave that up (118 sells; t = -0.7, within noise).
Decision IC: on the 35 days it traded, what it bought ranked against what it sold and left alone by a mean rank IC of -0.038 with the next five days' returns (IC IR -0.26, t = -1.5, within noise).
Holdings IC: the weights it held after each of 43 decision days had a mean rank IC of 0.001 with the next five days' returns (t = 0.0, within noise).
Factor exposures: market 0.34 (t 7.3), size 0.04 (t 1.0), growth -0.49 (t -8.4), momentum 0.06 (t 3.3); together they explain 39% of the daily variation (R²).
Of its +5.0% a year over T-bills (arithmetic mean): market +3.7%, momentum -1.3%, growth -1.2%, size +0.1%; the alpha left is +3.7% a year (t = 0.6, within noise).
Verdict: the exposures account for +1.3% a year of it, and the +3.7% a year left over is not significant: one period of daily returns cannot tell it from luck.
P&L: +$7,424 in all, +$5,700 from 41 positions and +$1,723 of interest on idle cash.
By holding period: 61+ days made the most (+$11,403, 12 positions); 21-60 days lost the most (-$4,577, 16 positions).
By sector: Energy made the most (+$3,418, 2 positions); Technology lost the most (-$2,637, 7 positions).
By stock: UNP made the most (+$2,338, 1 position); JPM lost the most (-$1,323, 4 positions).
By market regime of the previous close: risk-on 96 days +1.0% (SPY +2.0%); neutral 18 days -0.1% (SPY +4.5%); uncertain 97 days +5.9% (SPY +4.8%); risk-off 6 days +0.6% (SPY +0.3%).
News: 8 positions opened on news made +$1,911, the other 33 +$3,789; 12 positions closed on news made -$1,165; over the five days from the fill, news-triggered buys trailed SPY by 1.38% (t -1.2).

Concentration: the gains are spread out (the best two positions made 26% of them) but winners and losers nearly cancel, so the best two made 74% of the net P&L; the best was UNP bought 2026-01-05 and still open at the end, +$2,338. Had the best position made nothing, the run would have returned +5.1% instead of +7.4%.
